instructions: For each fact, read only the quotes and their context. Verdict `support` when the quotes alone state every part of the claim and of each value, with the same scope and qualifiers; `partial` when a part is missing; `not-supported` when the quotes say something else; `unsure` otherwise. A quote with a `heading` is the value line under that heading on the page: read the two together. Do not use what you remember. A clause, scope, condition or exception of the claim that appears only in the surrounding text and not in the quotes is missing: `partial`. A universal claim (always, every, each, all) whose exception stands in the surrounding text is `partial`. When the quotes support the claim but you can see a sentence that would support it better, still vote on the quotes you were given.

facts.claim: In the pricing example, 84.35 million replicated write request units are charged at $0.6250 per million, a charge of $52.72.

qualifiers.scope: per million replicated write request units, example Region
qualifiers.condition: price from a pricing example; replicated write units (rWCUs and rWRUs) are priced the same as single-Region write units (WCUs and WRUs)

evidence.title: Amazon DynamoDB Pricing | NoSQL Key-Value Database | Amazon Web Services
evidence.quote: You will consume 84.35 million replicated write request units (42,177,000 writes x 2 Regions), as described in Best Practices and Requirements for Managing Global Tables, resulting in a charge of $52.72 (84.35 million replicated write request units x $0.6250 per million).
evidence.context: Global tables: Now assume you choose to create a disaster recovery replica table in the US West (Oregon) Region. Assume that you add the replica in the US West (Oregon) Region when your table is 25 GB in size, resulting in $3.75 ($0.15 x 25 GB) of table restore charges. Also assume that your application traffic from earlier in this example is consistent for your global table. You will consume 84.35 million replicated write request units (42,177,000 writes x 2 Regions), as described in Best Practices and Requirements for Managing Global Tables, resulting in a charge of $52.72 (84.35 million replicated write request units x $0.6250 per million). You also store an additional 27 GB of data in your replicated table in the US West (Oregon) Region. The first 25 GB of storage are included in the AWS Free Tier in each AWS Region for tables using the DynamoDB Standard table class. The remaining 2 GB of storage are charged at $0.25 per GB, resulting in additional table storage cost of $0.50 for the month.
headings: On-demand pricing: Example with multiple additional features

evidence.title: Understanding Amazon DynamoDB billing for global tables
evidence.quote: Replicated write units (rWCUs and rWRUs) are priced the same as single-Region write units (WCUs and WRUs).
evidence.context:
Updates to Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs) are billed using the same units as single-Region DynamoDB tables, even if the base table for the GSI is a replica table. Update operations for GSIs are billed using the following units:
+ Write Request Units (WRUs) for on-demand capacity mode, where one WRU is charged for each write up to 1KB
+ Write Capacity Units (WCUs) for provisioned capacity mode, where one WCU provides one write per second for up to 1 KB

Replicated write units (rWCUs and rWRUs) are priced the same as single-Region write units (WCUs and WRUs). Replicated write (rWCU or rWRU) charges are incurred in every Region containing a replica table for the global table. DynamoDB does not charge cross-Region data transfer fees for replicating data between the Regions of a global table.

Read operations from single-Region tables and from replica tables use the following units::
+ Read Request Units (RRUs) for on-demand capacity mode, where one RRU is charged for each strongly consistent read up to 4KB
+ Read Capacity Units (RCUs) for provisioned tables, where one RCU provides one strongly consistent read per second for up to 4KB
headings: Understanding Amazon DynamoDB billing for global tables

facts.claim: DynamoDB Streams reads are charged in read request units. Each GetRecords API call is billed as a streams read request unit and returns up to 1 MB of data from DynamoDB Streams; streams read request units are separate from read requests on the table. GetRecords calls invoked through DynamoDB triggers on AWS Lambda are not charged (unless the functions run on Lambda Managed Instances), and GetRecords calls invoked by DynamoDB global tables are not charged.

values.display: returns up to 1 MB of data

qualifiers.condition: streams read request units are separate from table read requests; no charge for GetRecords calls invoked through DynamoDB triggers on AWS Lambda (except functions on Lambda Managed Instances) or invoked by DynamoDB global tables

evidence.title: Amazon DynamoDB Pricing | NoSQL Key-Value Database | Amazon Web Services
evidence.quote: DynamoDB charges for reading data from DynamoDB Streams in read request units. Each GetRecords API call is billed as a streams read request unit and returns up to 1 MB of data from DynamoDB Streams.
evidence.context:
### How pricing works for data movement (Streams, CDC, imports/exports to S3, data in/out)
DynamoDB Streams. DynamoDB charges for reading data from DynamoDB Streams in read request units. Each GetRecords API call is billed as a streams read request unit and returns up to 1 MB of data from DynamoDB Streams. Streams read request units are unique from read requests on your DynamoDB table. You are not charged for GetRecords API calls invoked through DynamoDB triggers on AWS Lambda, unless the functions are running on Lambda Managed Instances, in which case standard Streams charges will apply. Also, you are not charged for GetRecords API calls invoked by DynamoDB global tables.
Change Data Capture (CDC) for Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (KDS). DynamoDB charges for CDC for Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in CDC units. DynamoDB charges one CDC unit for each write (up to 1 KB). You pay only for the writes your application performs without having to manage throughput capacity on the table. Kinesis Data Streams charges still apply when you replicate DynamoDB changes to a Kinesis data stream. For more information, see Amazon Kinesis Data Streams pricing.
headings: How pricing works for data movement (Streams, CDC, imports/exports to S3, data in/out)
